evidence: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:51 adds `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` for a missing CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY. That matches the file's existing TOTP branch, which already throws in the same situations at lines 77, 82 and 90. The claim that 'the rest of the file uses return res.status' is wrong: the file already mixes both styles, and the new backup-code branch copies its sibling's pattern. All user-facing errors in the new branch (MissingBackupCodes :55, IncorrectBackupCode :63) use `return res.status(400).json`. An uncaught throw in a Next API route still becomes a 500. Cleaning up the whole file would be a separate refactor.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:148 sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypts. The array always has exactly 10 slots, created in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:61. It is replaced on every new setup and cleared on disable (disable.ts:107), so it cannot grow or 'pollute over time'. Lookup is `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` on a string, so a null slot can never match. Using splice or filter would work the same way and save only a few bytes. Nulling keeps the slot positions, which is a reasonable choice.

apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:221 `{twoFactorRequired ? !twoFactorLostAccess ? <TwoFactor center /> : <BackupCode center /> : null}`. This nested ternary has a negated inner condition, so it is harder to read than it needs to be. The repo's ESLint config has no no-nested-ternary rule. `{twoFactorRequired && (twoFactorLostAccess ? <BackupCode center /> : <TwoFactor center />)}` would be clearer. Readability only; behavior is correct.

next-auth-options.ts:137-145 and disable.ts:54-64: when all codes are null, the encrypted array is still non-empty, so the `!user.backupCodes` MissingBackupCodes branch does not run. The user just gets IncorrectBackupCode, so the observation is accurate. However, the suggested message ('regenerate codes') doesn't fit the PR: there is no regeneration feature, and codes are only re-created by running 2FA setup again (setup.ts:61). The missing_backup_codes text in common.json ('Please generate them in your settings') points to a flow that doesn't exist either. A clearer 'all backup codes used' message would be a small UX improvement, not a correctness bug.

apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:7 `export default function TwoFactor(...)`. This is a copy-paste leftover from apps/web/components/auth/TwoFactor.tsx. Because it is a default export, the imports (`import BackupCode from ...` in login.tsx:32 and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:8) still work. But the component shows up as 'TwoFactor' in React DevTools and stack traces, which is easy to confuse with the real TwoFactor. It's a one-word rename to `BackupCode`.

apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:71-75: resetState only clears password, errorMessage and step. The modal stays mounted at all times (apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:62, controlled by `open`), so backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri and secret stay in React state after closing, and the plaintext backup codes and TOTP secret remain in memory. That part is valid. Two points are overstated: (a) isSubmitting is already reset in handleSetup's finally block (:119), and (b) the old blob URL is already revoked before a new one is created (:98 `if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl)`), so URLs don't pile up. The step reset also prevents stale codes from being displayed again. Clearing backupCodes/secret/dataUri and revoking the URL in resetState would be a cheap hygiene fix.

apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:21-24 already does basic client-side checks: `required`, `minLength={10}`, `maxLength={11}` and a placeholder `XXXXX-XXXXX`. The server normalizes with `replaceAll("-", "")` and matches exactly (next-auth-options.ts:142, disable.ts:61), so a wrong format only produces IncorrectBackupCode and is not a correctness or security problem. Small gap: minLength 10 accepts 'XXXXX-XXXX' (9 code characters), and non-hex characters aren't rejected before sending. A `pattern` or zod regex would slightly improve UX, but it's optional.

apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:12 `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`. The only backup-code coverage is the download/copy/close steps in the setup test (:110-125), and those also have TODOs for checking file and clipboard content. The new auth paths, login with a backup code (next-auth-options.ts:131-157) and disabling with one (disable.ts:48-66), including one-time use, are not tested. The PR description admits tests weren't added. Since this is an authentication bypass path, tests are worth adding, but the reviewer only repeats what the author already flagged.

EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:163 defines `const formatBackupCode` after handleSetup (:77), which uses it at :94. handleSetup only runs from a form submit event, after the render body has finished, so formatBackupCode is always initialized by then. There's no temporal-dead-zone risk and no runtime bug. Moving it above handleSetup, or to module scope since it doesn't depend on component state, is purely about readability.

EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:99 `setBackupCodesUrl(URL.createObjectURL(textBlob))` has no cleanup on unmount. The only revoke is at :98 when a newer URL replaces it, and there is no useEffect cleanup. So when the user leaves the settings page, the last blob URL stays alive until the document unloads. The leak is bounded: at most one blob of about 120 bytes per mount, because earlier URLs are revoked. Technically correct but low impact. A `useEffect(() => () => { if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl) }, [backupCodesUrl])` would fix it.
